anomalies.observed: In the Capacitive Touch Button (TSC) block on the root sheet (PCB.kicad_sch, page 1, and continued on tile 2), the two hierarchical/net labels NET0004 (PB7, U2 pin 59) and NET0005 (PB5, U2 pin 57) both run into the same left terminal of the series resistor R4 (1 k). The 22 nF sampling capacitor C11 hangs off NET0004. This merges the electrode-drive pin PB5 with the sampling-capacitor pin PB7 into a single net at R4's input.
anomalies.expected: The specification keeps the two TSC pins separate: 'TSC_G2_IO2: U2 pin 57 (PB5) — R8 (1 kΩ series resistor) — A2 pin BTN' and 'TSC_G2_IO4: U2 pin 59 (PB7) — C14 (22 nF to GND)'. PB5 must connect to the electrode only through the series resistor, and PB7 must connect only to the sampling capacitor to GND; the two pins must not share a net.

evidence.quote: Capacitive Touch Button (TSC) block: 'NET0004' and 'NET0005' label boxes each with a wire terminating at the left lead of R4 (1k); C11 (22n) tied to NET0004 and GND; R4 right lead to A1 pin 1 (BTN), A1 pin 2 (SHLD) to GND (page 1 / tile 2).
TSC_G2_IO2: U2 pin 57 (PB5) — R8 (1 kΩ series resistor) — A2 pin BTN (the touch electrode); TSC_G2_IO4: U2 pin 59 (PB7) — C14 (22 nF to GND) — this is the TSC sampling capacitor for the group

anomalies.impact: Shorting the TSC sampling-capacitor pin (PB7) to the series-resistor/electrode pin (PB5) destroys the standard ST TSC topology (one sampling-C IO and one series-R sense IO per group). The touch electrode would not be sensed correctly and the capacitive button would likely fail to register presses.
